title: Tighter Uniform Bound for the Auxiliary Function g
summary: The derivation retains the constant 2, while numerics suggest values near 1 at large scale; prove a smaller rigorous uniform bound and quantify its improvement.

formal_statement.body: For parameters satisfying $0\leq\varepsilon\leq 1$ and $1\leq Mk\leq M-1$, define $g(\varepsilon,k,M)=\left(1+\frac{2\sqrt{1.25-\varepsilon}-\varepsilon}{2kM+\varepsilon-1}\right)^{\varepsilon}\left(1+\frac{2\sqrt{1.25-\varepsilon}}{2(1-k)M}\right)^{\varepsilon}$. The existing derivation avoids directly controlling $g$ and retains the looser constant $2$. Prove a rigorous upper bound $C<2$ such that $g(\varepsilon,k,M)\leq C$ uniformly over this parameter domain. Also quantify how the bound improves under a restriction $M>M_0$, ideally obtaining a constant close to $1$ for large $M_0$; a numerical search under $M>10^6$ reported $1$, but no analytic estimate was provided.

scope.domain: Analytic probability bounds arising in the security analysis of order-preserving encryption.
assumptions: The refined regime restricts M to be greater than M₀.
parameters: ε: constrained input and exponent in both factors of g
k: constrained input governing denominator terms in g
M: scale input appearing in both denominator terms
C: sought uniform upper-bound constant below 2
M₀: lower threshold for studying improvement as M grows
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove a uniform upper bound below 2 for g and quantify its improvement when M is bounded below, ideally obtaining a constant near 1 for large thresholds.

progress.summary: The paper retains the looser constant 2 and proposes directly bounding g to tighten it. A numerical search reports 1 when M exceeds one million, but no analytic estimate is given.
